The overbooking is done intentionally. Many airlines do it.

Every flight is virtually guaranteed to have a certain amount of ticket holders that don't show up, or miss the flight or what have you. By overselling the flight, the airline gets to cash in twice on those peoples seats, making them more money. Had they not oversold the flight, those seats remain empty, and while the airline isn't "losing" money, they're missing the chance to make more.

I work in a hotel and we do sort of the same thing. We'll overbook the property buy a certain amount of rooms depending on the date. We know for a fact that on any given day when we're sold out, there are sure to be a few no shows. Now, we can still charge these people for not cancelling but all it takes is a call to their cc company and we get a charge back. Overbooking ensures that we not only get full property value for the night, but that we also get to "double charge" some rooms.

So I understand it. Is it fair to customers? Not really, but I understand the practice. It makes perfect sense from the standpoint of the business.
